title: HRV is the readout, breathing is the remote control
body: Heart rate variability is a cheap, daily-trackable proxy for how activated the body's central stress circuit is — and slow, paced breathing is one of the few levers that moves it in real time, for free. Covers the HPA-axis mechanism, which stress stats actually hold up, resonance-frequency breathing with an interactive pacer, and a near-free chest-strap-band hack.

title: HRV & Resonance Breathing
body: A working reference for daily practice and sleep. Resonance breathing at 6 breaths/min, dosage that actually builds a habit, and three distinct tools for sleep — including what to do at 2:30am and what not to do at bedtime.

title: Heart health: a genetics-first framework
body: Most heart-health content assumes lifestyle is the main lever. It isn't, for everyone — some people do everything right and still build plaque, because the real driver is genetic. Two anonymised case studies, a testing toolkit, and where cardiology guidance is solid versus still genuinely contested.

title: Sun angle, infrared, and latitude
body: Low sun feels different from midday sun, and there's real physics behind it — but the popular story about latitude and infrared has the direction backwards. Covers sun-angle spectral shifts, photobiomodulation, full-spectrum saunas, and where the science actually stops.

title: EZ water: the fourth phase
body: Most of the water in your cells isn't ordinary liquid water. Gerald Pollack's decades of research argue for a structured, negatively-charged "fourth phase" — H₃O₂ — that forms against every surface in the body, with the same physics driving water up a 100-metre tree.

title: The four ways to use Claude
body: Chat, Projects, Cowork, and Claude Code are four different products built for different contexts. Understanding which to reach for — and when to switch — is what turns Claude from occasionally useful into genuinely transformative.

title: Share buying rules
body: A disciplined framework for entering, managing, and exiting positions — built to slow down impulse decisions and protect capital. Covers entry rules, dip-buying criteria, stop discipline, the YouTube tip rule, macro awareness, and a weekly rhythm.

title: Boredom is underrated
body: Everyone's trying to optimise their way out of doing nothing. But boredom is where your brain actually gets to wander — it's the only state where you have an original thought instead of reacting to someone else's content. We've accidentally scheduled it out of existence.

title: The problem with productivity porn
body: There's an entire genre of content about how to be more productive that is, paradoxically, the biggest threat to your productivity. Watching a 45-minute video on the Pomodoro technique is not the same as actually doing the thing.

title: Restaurants should show you the fridge
body: A restaurant tour of the walk-in fridge before you sit down would tell you everything you need to know about the kitchen. How organised it is, how fresh things look, whether the shelves are labelled. Better than any review.
